Subject: Azure private plan — PCI scope and SLA request

Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro call yesterday. Fortuna is evaluating Redwood for an Azure private plan to support our card-processing workloads. The security team flagged two items we need before procurement can move forward: a short PCI scope statement for the private deployment, and an SLA exhibit that anchors uptime and incident response commitments for production traffic.

Can you share the draft SLA and any evidence you have on PCI posture (attestation or assessment) so our GRC folks can start the review? Ideally by end of week.

Also: who should we expect to see on the contract/redline distribution?

Appreciate it —
Alex Byrne
Head of Procurement
Fortuna Bank
procurement@fortunabank.com

Attachments: none

Date: 2027-04-11T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Azure private plan — PCI scope and SLA request

Alex — thanks for the note and the clear ask. Quick replies inline and attached:

- PCI posture: attaching our PCI attestation summary (PDF). It covers environment segmentation for private deployments and controls mapping.
- SLA exhibit: attaching a first-cut SLA_Exhibit that maps uptime, severity definitions, and response windows for Dedicated/Private modes.

What you should expect from us for contract circulation: myself and Jordan on commercial terms; Rishi will handle legal redlines on the MSA/SLA exhibits; Priya will own billing/entitlement items. Please loop any contract or purchasing contacts and we’ll sync on the review cadence.

Next steps I propose:
1) You and your GRC team review the PCI attestation and call out any gaps by EOD Thursday.
2) We receive initial redlines to the SLA exhibit in DocuSign/Word and we’ll respond within 48 hours.
3) If needed, schedule a 30-minute technical call with our security engineering team (cc: rishi for availability).

Attachments (2): SLA_Exhibit_vA_redwood_20270411.pdf (pdf), PCI_Attestation_Redwood_2023.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Azure private plan — PCI scope and SLA request

Kimberly / team — quick read of the SLA exhibit and a few proposed guardrails from Legal that we should surface to Fortuna before they send formal redlines. Inline comments: 

- "Force majeure" clause: suggest tightening to limit length of relief for sustained unavailability that impacts card processing (Proposed: carveout for scheduled maintenance with 72-hour notice; severe outage relief capped at 14 days).
- "Data residency / access" section: add explicit statement that Redwood does not export payloads to third-party analytics vendors without written consent.
- "Escalation path / credits": propose a defined credit table (p50/p95 latency breaches are tricky — prefer uptime/incident severity credits).

I noted a few items that will likely be redlined by procurement: indemnity caps tied to subscription fees, and an audit clause for PCI evidence. Recommend we offer: (a) a SOC2-type report for initial review, (b) a mutually agreed audit window for high-risk customers (restricted to approved controls and with cost sharing).

Jordan — happy to join a short call with Alex if they want to walk the legal asks. Priya — confirm if the credit table below is acceptable from a billing/finance perspective: "Severity 1: 99.95% monthly uptime — credit 10% of monthly fees; Severity 2: 99.5% — credit 5%" (draft only).

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
